name: Neptune
fact: Voyager 2 flew past Neptune in 1989 after a 12-year journey. It remains the only spacecraft ever to visit.
bio: Windiest planet — 2,100 km/h surface winds. Discovered by mathematical prediction before direct observation, because Uranus's orbit showed an unseen gravitational influence.

science_sections.why: At 30.07 AU mean distance, Neptune is so far that a single one-way light signal takes 4 hours each way. Voyager 2 needed 12 years to reach it.
Triton is the only large moon in the solar system with a retrograde orbit — strong evidence it was captured from the Kuiper Belt, not formed with Neptune.
Neptune's gentle 0.0086 eccentricity gives an orbit so circular that perihelion–aphelion swing is under 200 million km on a 30-AU semi-major axis — a 1.4 % variation.
Voyager 2 (1989 flyby) remains the only spacecraft to have visited Neptune. No mission to the system is currently funded or in flight.
